A layout says where shapes are. A simulation also needs to know which shapes
are conductors, which conductors share an electrical Net, where a port connects,
and which materials occupy the surrounding space.

## Entity, occurrence and Net

An **Entity** is a named source part, such as a pad or a ground conductor.
Placing a component creates an **occurrence** of its local Entities. A named
path distinguishes repeated parts before flattening. The study assigns those
qualified Entities to electrical **Nets**; similar labels or a visual impression
of contact do not perform that assignment.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  C["Local Entities + ports"] --> O["Named occurrence"]
  O --> N["Final Nets"]
  P["PDK materials + stack"] --> S["GeometryPlan snapshot"]
  N --> S
  S --> B["Backend model"]
```

The PDK supplies material identity, fabrication level, thickness and host-volume
facts. The component supplies local polygons and selectors. GeometryPlan
combines the actual placed source with a final Net map and an outer vacuum
region. Preparing it produces detached GDS, stack and normalized geometry.
Changing shared geometry requires a new snapshot.

A backend may combine several source members into one mesh group or field
integral. Those computational groups do not erase source identity or promise
one reported value for every Entity. In the existing Xmon example,
`chip/device/D1_XMON_PAD` is an Entity and `xmon_pad` is its assigned Net;
several Ground members can share a native group.

## Regions and boundaries

The vacuum envelope is part of the field model, not the camera view. Substrate,
vacuum gaps and conductor bodies retain their own identities. Boundary conditions
belong to the physical calculation: the same snapshot can be used with different
exterior conditions and produce different experiments.

## Explicit curved boundaries

Component source can attach authored line, circular-arc, interpolation-spline,
or B-spline chains to selected Entity boundaries. A caller can also explicitly
select a curve reconstruction for a GDS boundary. The source snapshot retains
the polygon source and curve declarations; placing an occurrence transforms
the ordered curve chain with its Entity. Curve intent does not assign a Net,
and SCGSim does not smooth polygon edges implicitly. Polygon-only inputs remain
polygonal.

Palace Routes A and B lower active curve intent. Route C and AEDT planar
preparation do not support curves. The [GeometryPlan contract](../geometry-sgb.qmd)
describes how to author a chain or select GDS boundary segments, and how those
boundaries retain their Entity and occurrence identities.

## A shared source has a specific reach

Palace Electrostatic/Eigenmode and source-first HFSS Eigenmode consume a
GeometryPlan snapshot. Ordinary GDS-based HFSS workflows use explicit layer
and object bindings. Q3D v3 uses explicit body rings, Z intervals, materials
and final Net membership; its source-first C/G frontend can consume a
GeometryPlan snapshot. Native Q3D body lowering remains **CONVERGING**. Q2D
uses cross-section rectangles and conductor groups; there is no implicit
GeometryPlan-to-Q2D slice.

Read [model approximations](model-and-numerics.qmd) next, or use the
[GeometryPlan contract](../geometry-sgb.qmd#component-to-backend-geometry-contract)
for exact authoring rules. The [tutorials](../examples.qmd) show the sequence.
